 Mr. Rakesh Kumar, Adv.
 For the Respondent/s : Ms. Abha Singh, APP  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER 3 14-03-2024 1.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned APP for the State.
2. The matter has been placed before this Court for consideration of the appellant's bail prayer made under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. and suspension of his sentence during the pendency of the appeal.

3. This appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 07.12.2023 and order of sentence dated 16.12.2023 passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VIII-cum-Special Judge (POCSO Act), Patna in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No.
94/2018 arising out of Bhagwanganj P.S. Case No. 31 of 2018, whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted for the offences Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text:

dt.14-03-2024 punishable under Sections 363 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced for the said offences.

4. Mr. Ramakant Sharma, learned senior counsel for the appellant submits that the major punishment awarded upon the appellant is ten years of rigorous imprisonment for the offence under section 6 of POCSO Act, against which the appellant has undergone and served about six years in jail and there is no chance of early hearing of his appeal.

Learned counsel further submits that the trial Karu Yadav @ Karu Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67005658/
1 court has ignored the discrepancy in the date of birth of the victim, as initially, she disclosed her age as 13 years, however, in the school register, her age appears to be 15 years and in the marriage certificate issued by the Surya Temple, her age was mentioned as 19 years and the Doctor, PW-8, did not find any sign of injury on the person of the victim and the allegations levelled by the victim are completely absurd, in fact the victim and the appellant disappeared from their house and entered into inter-caste marriage which was opposed by the family members of the victim, leading to the institution of the FIR of the present matter.
5.

sentences.text: Ms. Abha Singh, learned APP appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.538 of 2024(3) dt.14-03-2024 6.

Considering the above submissions and mainly taking into account the appellant's custody period which he has undergone and served till date and unlikelihood of his appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future, this Court is inclined to accept the appellant's bail prayer.

Accordingly, let the appellant named-above be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-VIII-cum-Special Judge (POCSO Act), Patna in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No. 94/2018 arising out of Bhagwanganj P.S. Case No. 31 of 2018.
7. List this appeal under appropriate heading in due course.
(Shailendra Singh, J) annu/-
